papers.title: Rebrightening in the Radio: Secondary Flares from Tidal Disruption Events AT2019ehz and AT2019eve
papers.abstract: We present the discovery of new secondary delayed radio flares from two tidal disruption events (TDEs), AT2019ehz and AT2019eve from observations ranging 1-18 GHz using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array. For AT2019ehz, we find a secondary flare in radio emission began at 1545 days post-disruption, 770 days after the first radio flare detected at 775 days post-disruption, and for AT2019eve the secondary flare was detected at 1594 days post-disruption, 825 days after its initial radio detection at 769 days post-disruption. Through spectral modeling of the multi-frequency observations, we extract physical parameters of the new flares to constrain the origin of the rebrightening. We find the secondary flare of AT2019ehz is likely produced by a second outflow launched at roughly 1000 days. For AT2019eve, the secondary flare reveals unexpected spectral evolution with a self-absorbed peak increasing from 1325 to 2173 days post-disruption, which is not well explained with most models of expanding outflows and instead suggests a more complex physical geometry. This inconclusive origin of AT2019eve highlights the need for more complex models to explain observed TDE radio evolution.

papers.title: How to find regular black-hole islands in the swamp
papers.abstract: An infinite tower of higher-curvature corrections is expected to lead to regular black-hole solutions. We assume that this regular behavior does not abruptly arise, but gradually builds up with each successive order of the effective field theory of gravity. In addition, we assume that the effective field theory comes with a single scale of singularity-resolving new physics. We translate this assumption into a monotonicity requirement for deviations of the metric functions from a Schwarzschild black hole. Under these assumptions, conditions can be formulated which trace the increase of ``less singular'' black-hole behavior on and outside of the black-hole horizon within the regime of validity of the effective field theory. These conditions constrain the effective field theory coefficients. To exemplify this construction, we motivate five specific conditions and find a corresponding island of black hole regularity conditions at order eight in the effective field theory. We also explore whether string theory as well as asymptotically safe gravity lie on this island.

papers.title: Improved constraints on axion inflation with the new code AxioGen: an efficient generator of curvature perturbations
papers.abstract: Axion inflation, in which a pseudoscalar inflaton couples to a $U(1)$ gauge field via a Chern-Simons interaction, has garnered significant interest due to its rich phenomenology. The power spectrum and bispectrum for this model are often parametrized by functions known as $f_2$ and $f_3$, respectively. Previous work computed $f_2$ and $f_3$ using an approximation for the gauge field mode functions. While these approximate solutions are fairly accurate ($\mathcal{O}(10\%)$) for large values of the model parameter $\xi$, which controls gauge field particle production, our recent work has shown them to be quite inaccurate for smaller values of $\xi$. We present new fitting functions for $f_2$ and $f_3$ that are significantly more accurate than those previously used. We use these functions to place new constraints on $\xi$ and also set lower bounds for the energy scale of the axion gauge field coupling for $\phi^{1/3}$ and $\phi^{2/3}$ inflationary potentials. Additionally, we present a new public code to efficiently generate realizations of the primordial curvature perturbation for axion inflation in the weak backreaction regime. This code enables numerical computation of higher order correlators and provides a novel path to initial conditions for large-scale structure formation.

papers.title: Matching 2HDM to HEFT in triple Higgs boson production from WBF
papers.abstract: In this work we compare the Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT) predictions with the Two Higgs Doublet Model (2HDM) predictions for triple Higgs production via $WW \rightarrow hhh$ scattering, under the hypothesis of very heavy Higgs bosons $H$, $A$, and $H^\pm$, and assuming the lightest one $h$ has the observed mass in the experiments, $m_h \simeq 125$ GeV. By requiring the matching of the two corresponding scattering amplitudes for this $WW \rightarrow hhh$ process in the limit of very heavy mass for these bosons, we find the solutions for the leading order HEFT coefficients. Concretely, we determine the coefficients $a$, $b$, $c$, $\kappa_3$ and $\kappa_4$ defining the effective interactions $WWh$, $WWhh$, $WWhhh$, $hhh$ and $hhhh$, respectively, in terms of the 2HDM input parameters, $c_{\beta-\alpha}$, $\tan \beta$ and $m_{12}$. We will also compare these solutions with the corresponding solutions found for the case of double Higgs production. The solutions presented here for the matched coefficients summarize the non-decoupling effects from the heavy modes, $H$, $A$ and $H^\pm$ in the scattering process $WW \rightarrow hhh$ and provide the most relevant contributions to the cross section $\sigma(WW \rightarrow hhh)$ that do not decrease as inverse powers of the heavy masses. In the last part, we will also discuss the numerical predictions of the cross section $\sigma(WW \rightarrow hhh)$ in terms of the HEFT-matched coefficients. The focus of this discussion is set on the big gap between the HEFT-matched prediction and the SM prediction due to the non-decoupling behaviour occurring whenever misalignment is assumed in the 2HDM, i.e. for $c_{\beta-\alpha} \neq 0$. This big gap could serve as potential signals of the 2HDM heavy modes, $H$, $A$ and $H^\pm$, at future high energy colliders, even if they are too heavy and cannot be produced at these colliders.

papers.abstract: Euclid is a European Space Agency mission mapping the extragalactic sky, aiming to provide the most-accurate 3D view of the Universe at optical and near-infrared wavelengths, by measuring the photometric redshifts of billions of galaxies. Within the Euclid Consortium, this task is executed by the PHZ Organisation Unit. PHZ takes as input the multi-wavelength photometry of Euclid and ground-based data, and returns as output the source classification, photometric redshifts for the Euclid core science (i.e., cosmology), and photometric redshifts plus physical parameters and absolute magnitudes for non-cosmological science. As part of the first Euclid Data Release (DR1), we describe the details of the DR1 pipeline for non-cosmological science, along with the released data products, and their validation. The non-cosmological science data products are obtained with NNPZ, a nearest-neighbour algorithm developed within PHZ that infers the properties of each target galaxy from its closest matches, in colour-magnitude space, within a reference sample of galaxies with known redshifts and physical parameters. We built this reference sample from Euclid observations of COSMOS, one of the Euclid Auxiliary Fields, labelling each galaxy with redshifts and physical parameters derived from the COSMOS2020 multi-wavelength photometry, consistently with the Euclid core-science results. Combined with the adjustments and priors required to generalise the results across the entire extragalactic sky, this approach yields high-quality and internally consistent data products. We tested the performance using both internal metrics and comparisons to ancillary data sets (e.g., COSMOS2020, 3D-HST, and DESI) and scaling relations (e.g., the star-forming main sequence); the results are in line with expectations and pre-DR1 simulations for both the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep Fields.

papers.title: The ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR): Initial Data Release (DR1)
papers.abstract: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.

papers.title: Cubic Curvature Deformations to the Kerr Black Hole Shadow
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. Starting from a perturbatively corrected Kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. Using a Hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. We find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the Kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. In particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. We validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical Kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. Our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.

papers.title: Numerical Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes with Higher-Order Mass Corrections
papers.abstract: Inspired by noncommutative geometry and quintessence, we construct a new class of asymptotically anti-de Sitter black hole solutions characterized by a higher-order mass deformation term $\frac{aM^{n-1}}{r^n}$ involving two parameters, $a$ and $n$. Due to analytical difficulties, we approach the underlying thermodynamics through parallel programming simulations using CUDA codes. By considering models with $n=3$, $n=4$, and $n=5$, we numerically study certain thermodynamic properties, including the stability, the $P$-$v$ criticality, and the phase transitions.

papers.title: Anatomy of LyC Escape in MEGATRON: Connecting Feedback Physics to Demographics, Leakage Timescales, and Explorations of ISM Density as a Tracer of Escape Fraction
papers.abstract: Constraining the Lyman Continuum (LyC) escape fraction ($f_{\rm esc}$) of high-redshift galaxies is essential to connect the abundant populations revealed by \textit{JWST} to cosmic reionization. We investigate this interplay using {\small MEGATRON}, a suite of zoom simulations with detailed radiation/chemistry and varied feedback prescriptions. We find that feedback physics simultaneously regulates UV source counts, LyC escape fractions, and escaping ionizing luminosities ($\dot{N}_{\rm ion,esc}$), producing different reionization histories. These differences are governed by the delay between a starburst and LyC escape: efficient early feedback and lower-density environments enable photons to escape while pre-supernovae stellar populations remain strongly ionizing. Consequently, models that produce fewer UV-bright galaxies yield earlier LyC escape and reionize sooner than models with more abundant UV sources and delayed LyC emission. Furthermore, UV-faint galaxies follow a common physical sequence in ISM structure with increasing $f_{\rm esc}$ irrespective of feedback physics: stronger leakers ($1\%\leq f_{\rm esc}\leq 50\%$) exhibit evidence of strong photoionization and SNe feedback alongside post-starburst star formation histories, while extreme leakers ($f_{\rm esc}\geq 50\%$) have also cleared their cold/dense ISM. We find that electron densities inferred from the $\rm [O\,{II}]\,\lambda\lambda3727$ doublet are a candidate diagnostic of $f_{\rm esc}$, with lower densities around $\rm H~{\small II}$ regions selecting stronger leakers. Moreover, this density can trace the early evolution of $f_{\rm esc}$, whereas UV slope-based calibrations over-predict $\dot{N}_{\rm ion,esc}$ for individual young galaxies by up to two orders of magnitude. Overall, the delayed duty cycle of LyC leakage must be accounted for when UV source counts are interpreted in the context of reionization.

papers.title: Gray-body factors: Method matters II, WKB vs GrayHawk
papers.abstract: We present a systematic comparison between two independent approaches for the computation of gray-body factors. A fully numerical integration of the radial scattering equation, as implemented in GrayHawk, and one based on the WKB approximation. We consider four black hole geometries and scalar, fermionic, and vector perturbations, comparing the corresponding gray-body factors, primary Hawking emission spectra, and Page evaporation factors. As expected for high-frequency and large $l$ regimes, the two methods provide excellent agreement. At low frequencies, however, systematic discrepancies emerge and become particularly pronounced for nearly-extremal black holes. Systematic discrepancies are also met when considering effective geometric potentials characterized by the presence of more than one peak. A significant difference between the two approaches is also found in their computational cost, highlighting their complementary nature.

papers.title: Euclid First Data Release 1 (DR1) - Data release overview
papers.abstract: This paper describes the contents of the Euclid First Data Release (DR1), together with the set of papers that document the data-processing and the data products. DR1 consists of two parts: first `DR1-Foundation', releasing images, spectra, and catalogues in November 2026. Second, the shear measurements and the `Level~3' products required for cosmological analyses will be added in June 2027 to complete the full DR1. This data set contains around a billion catalogued objects, mainly from the Euclid Wide Survey (1975\,deg$^2$) and the Euclid Deep Fields (77\,deg$^2$)

papers.title: FOORT: Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing
papers.abstract: We present FOORT (Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing), an open C++ code for ray-tracing images of black holes and other compact objects in arbitrary spacetimes. FOORT is designed to offer flexibility and can handle horizons, naked singularities and numerical metrics, allowing it to ray-trace numerous different metrics including Kerr and other black holes, as well as horizonless objects such as fuzzballs and boson stars. New metrics, analytical or numerical, can be added with minimal effort, and geodesics are initialized at the camera without reference to conserved quantities, so no special structure of the metric is required. Besides the intensity observed from a geometrically and optically thin equatorial disk, FOORT is set up to track a number of diagnostics along each geodesic, such as the number of equatorial crossings and the radius of closest approach. Its adaptive mesh can refine the image on any of these diagnostics, efficiently resolving narrow features such as higher-order photon rings. Accompanying Python tools convert the output into images and interferometric visibility amplitudes. We describe the main features of the code, validate it against analytic results in the Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, demonstrate it on several non-Kerr metrics, and characterize its scaling with the number of OpenMP threads. FOORT is lightweight, requiring only C++17 and OpenMP, and has already been used in a number of studies of black hole and compact-object imaging. The code is publicly available in a GitHub repository.

papers.title: Machine-Learning Reconstruction of Intergalactic Medium Column-Density Maps from Observed Ly$\alpha$ Emission Cubes
papers.abstract: Understanding the large-scale structure of the intergalactic medium (IGM) is essential for studying galaxy evolution, particularly at $z \sim 2$--$6$, when cold filaments in the cosmic web are considered a primary mechanism for fueling galaxy growth. At these redshifts, Ly$\alpha$ emission shifts into the optical regime and serves as the primary tracer of diffuse IGM for ground-based integral field units (IFUs). However, detections remain limited by low signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) and the complexities of resonant scattering. We present a proof-of-concept machine-learning framework to reconstruct IGM gas column-density maps from noisy Ly$\alpha$ IFU emission cubes. Using Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI) observations of $z \sim 2.3$ protoclusters as a case study, we train a custom convolutional neural network (CNN), the Column Density Estimator (CDE), on a simulated dataset combining IllustrisTNG100 with simplified radiative-transfer calculations and an approximate treatment of KCWI noise. The CDE successfully reconstructs broad filamentary structures in the simulated test set under these adopted assumptions. Applied to observed KCWI data, the CDE predicts gas column-density maps containing filamentary structures extending over $\gtrsim 40''$ ($\sim 1$ comoving Mpc), consistent with an IGM interpretation. The observed reconstructions remain conditional on the adopted models. These results illustrate the potential of the CDE framework for connecting diffuse Ly$\alpha$ observations with simulations of the IGM.

papers.title: Satellite pairs in the Local Group: from spatial clustering to dynamical associations in observations and $\Lambda$CDM simulations
papers.abstract: We investigate the incidence and physical nature of satellite galaxy pairs in the Local Group using updated observational data for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31), together with analogues from the HESTIA constrained cosmological simulations. Our comparison uses three distinct simulated Local Group analogues drawn from the HESTIA suite, allowing us to assess the observed pair statistics against multiple cosmological realisations of the Local Group environment. We identify close nearest-neighbour associations by comparing the observed satellite distributions with isotropic populations that reproduce the radial distributions of each host, and investigate their physical nature using line-of-sight velocities, proper motions, and gravitational binding estimates. We find that the MW exhibits a significant excess of close satellite associations relative to isotropic expectations, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim53\%$, nearly twice that found in the simulated analogues ($\sim17$-$27\%$). This excess persists after applying a stellar mass cut ($M_\star > 10^4\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) to match the resolution limits of the simulations. In contrast, the M31 satellite system is broadly consistent with isotropy, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim28\%$. However, only a minority of pair candidates exhibit coherent kinematics or are likely to be gravitationally bound, indicating that most represent transient alignments or remnants of common group infall rather than long-lived binary satellites. These results suggest that the MW hosts an unusually rich population of phase-space-correlated satellites, likely reflecting its recent accretion history, whereas M31 is more consistent with typical $\Lambda$CDM expectations.

papers.title: Recurrent Fourier Neural Operator for Event-by-Event Relativistic Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Relativistic hydrodynamics is a powerful tool to simulate the evolution of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but event-by-event simulations are computationally demanding, especially for Bayesian analyses. We develop a recurrent Fourier neural operator (rFNO) that emulates the evolution of $(2+1)$-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics. Three networks are trained on the $32\times32$, $64\times64$, and $128\times128$ lattices using profiles of the same \textsc{VISH2+1} hydrodynamic events up to $\tau-\tau_0=4.8~\mathrm{fm}/c$. The networks trained on the coarser lattices are then directly evaluated on the $128\times128$ lattice without retraining, while the $128\times128$ network provides the native-resolution reference. A comparison with the \textsc{VISH2+1} results shows that the rFNO predictions across resolutions nicely capture the magnitude and structures of the temperature profiles, and describe the event-by-event eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$ ($n=2,3,4$), the momentum anisotropy $\varepsilon_p$, and their time evolution within the supervised proper-time interval. After the recurrent continuation to $\tau-\tau_0=6.4~\mathrm{fm}/c$, the relative errors of the predicted $\varepsilon_n$ and $\varepsilon_p$ remain within about $10\%$. These results demonstrate that the rFNO realizes zero-shot super-resolution predictions for relativistic hydrodynamics and can be recurrently continued beyond the supervised interval.

papers.title: Binary black holes with non-orthogonal reference metrics
papers.abstract: To our knowledge, numerical relativity (NR) simulations in the covariant moving-puncture formalism have only been performed with orthogonal reference metrics. Here, we demonstrate a new general non-orthogonal reference 3-metric implementation. We first validate this reference metric implementation by numerically evolving the exact Kasner initial data with a fisheye-style reference 3-metric, demonstrating numerical results that converge to the exact solution with increasing grid resolution. Next, we validate our approach by evolving binary black holes (BBHs) in the moving-puncture formulation, from inspiral through merger and ringdown. Even with a large deformation in the reference geometry, introduced to allow a large change in grid refinement to enable the simulation to span the relevant length scales, from high resolutions near the BHs to low resolutions in the wave zone, no pathologies are observed. Smooth waveforms for up to $\ell=8$ are extracted on a grid without mesh refinement boundaries. We demonstrate the flexibility of tuning structured grids through the reference metric by employing spheroidal modifications of the spherical fisheye map to reduce the number of grid points in the $z$ direction when the orbit is in the $xy$-plane. These results support the use of smoothly derefined structured grids for BBH evolutions.

papers.title: LHAASO's Peanut source is a laboratory for studying magnetic fields in the Milky Way
papers.abstract: Recently, the LHAASO Collaboration reported gamma-ray emission from the Peanut-shaped source (Peanut), which extends over $4.5^\circ$ parallel to the Galactic plane at $b=-17.5^\circ$. The source is associated with the millisecond pulsar PSR J0218+4232, located at the eastern edge of the Peanut, at a distance of 3 kpc from the Earth and 0.9 kpc from the Galactic plane. Its location and bright gamma-ray emission above 25 TeV make it a natural laboratory for studying the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) in the transition region between the Galactic plane and halo. We interpret the observed emission as inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by electrons propagating along the large-scale GMF, accounting for turbulence through two models: Kolmogorov and Goldreich-Sridhar (GS). These models correspond to diffusive and ballistic particle propagation, respectively. While the GS case naturally provides conditions for one-sided gamma-ray emission, in the Kolmogorov case assumptions of one-sided particle injection and magnetic mirror at the source are necessary. We find that, in the Kolmogorov scenario, the Peanut's hotspots are likely associated with magnetic bottling, whereas in the GS scenario, they are related to magnetic field line geometry. Both models yield constraints on the GMF at the location of the Peanut.

papers.title: Tau polarization, new physics and CP violation in $\nu_\tau$-nucleus hyperon production
papers.abstract:
Charged-current interactions of the $	au$ neutrino are the least constrained sector of the Standard Model (SM) flavour structure, and the polarisation of the produced $	au$ lepton probes new-physics (NP) couplings, including CP-violating ones. Hyperon and charmed-baryon production gives access to the $u	o s$ and $d	o c$ transitions, but any measurement would be made on nuclei, which calls for a proper treatment of nuclear effects. We therefore study the sequential reactions $
u_	au\,{}^A Z	o	au^-(	o\pi^-
u_	au)\,\Lambda_c^+ X$ and $ ar
u_	au\,{}^A Z	o	au^+ (	o\pi^+ ar
u_	au)\,\Lambda X$ within the impulse approximation. The energy and angular distributions of the pion, which encode the $	au$ polarization, are derived for an arbitrary nuclear hole spectral function. As for free nucleons, an azimuthal pion asymmetry with respect to the plane spanned by the neutrino and the outgoing baryon is shown to remain. This is a CP-odd observable that vanishes in the SM, so that a nonzero value would signal CP violation irrespective of the hadronic form factors. Local Fermi gas results for ${}^{16}$O show that nuclear effects lower the reaction thresholds but leave the pion distributions, and hence the polarization information, close to their free-nucleon form. For representative NP scenarios the predicted asymmetries are at the percent level or below, with a magnitude that, in the $\Lambda$ channel, depends strongly on the transition form factors.

papers.title: Frequency-dependent time delays in Sgr A* from a broadband VLA observation
papers.abstract: Frequency-dependent radio time delays have been measured in Sgr A* light curves, with higher-frequency emission generally leading lower-frequency emission. These lags have been interpreted in terms of an organized jet-like outflow, expanding plasma components, or magnetic-flux eruptions, although their origin and recurrence remain uncertain. We aim to search for and quantify frequency-dependent radio time delays in a new high-cadence Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observation of Sgr A*. Using the improved broad 12-37 GHz frequency coverage, we measured the timing of the dominant variability feature and compared the resulting lag-wavelength slope with previous measurements. Sgr A* was observed with the VLA on 28 May 2022 in the Ku, K, and Ka bands over a 6-hour track. We extracted both band-averaged and 2 GHz subband light curves and measured the delays using a peak-time method and a locally normalized cross-correlation function. The light curves show one broad variability feature, with the maximum occurring progressively later at lower observing frequencies. Both timing methods recover a positive lag-wavelength relation, with a slope of order 40 min/cm. This value agrees with time lag results reported over more than 15 years from the first VLA observations at 22-43 GHz to later multifrequency VLA and ALMA campaigns. The sign and magnitude of the estimated delay are consistent with outward propagation through an optically thick synchrotron-emitting region. The recurrence of comparable delays over almost two decades suggests that frequency-dependent radio lags are a persistent feature of Sgr A* variability. Broadband, multi-epoch VLA monitoring of Sgr A* provides a useful probe of its radio variability, but robust lag measurements require high cadence and improved (u,v) coverage of both Sgr A* and the surrounding extended emission such as by combining different VLA configurations.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$\alpha$ Forest at the Field Level
papers.abstract: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Ly-alpha) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.

The decay $K^+ightarrow\pi^+

papers.title: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Top Taggers from JetClass to a Full-Simulation $Z'\to t\bar{t}$ Search: Transfer, Extrapolation, Sensitivity and Inference Cost
papers.abstract: Searches for heavy resonances decaying to \(t\bar{t}\) test physics beyond the Standard Model at the TeV scale, and their reach depends on how well boosted top jets are identified. Machine-learning top taggers are usually compared on fast-simulation samples without pileup and in a narrow jet-\(p_T\) window, so a benchmark ranking does not directly show how much each tagger adds to a real search. This study trains seven taggers under identical conditions on JetClass. They are a boosted decision tree, two image-based networks, ParticleNet, and three particle transformers (ParT, UParT, and GloParT). The taggers are then applied without retraining to a \(Z'\to t\bar{t}\) search with \(m_{Z'}\) between 1.2 and 2.5~TeV, using 2016 CMS Open Data simulated with Geant4 and realistic pileup. The overall benchmark order of the taggers is preserved. However, taggers with similar area under the ROC curve (AUC) differ by up to a factor of three in jet-level discovery significance. The particle transformers extend the mass reach of the search by \(400~\mathrm{GeV}\), and their lead grows with resonance mass. This gain is seen in fully merged top jets and is associated with stable performance at jet \(p_T\) above the training range. Pileup has only a minor effect on all taggers. A small convolutional network achieves competitive discrimination at a much lower computational cost. The gaps between tagger groups hold under retraining and within statistical uncertainties. The results show that a tagger must be chosen on its kinematic coverage, the working point of the analysis, its discovery sensitivity and its cost, and not on its benchmark score alone.

papers.title: Automated identification of dipole mixed-modes in red-giant stars
papers.abstract: Dipole mixed modes probe the internal structure of red giants by carrying information from both the convective envelope and the radiative core. Hence, identifying these modes allows for the determination of evolutionary states and stellar interior conditions. This identification typically relies on comparing observed frequencies with theoretical ones derived from the mixed-mode asymptotic relation. However, the process is challenging due to parameter-space degeneracies, stellar rotation, as well as missing modes and spurious peaks in the power density spectrum. In this work, we aim to develop an automated method for identifying dipole mixed modes, suitable for large-scale asteroseismic analyses. We introduce a metric that measures the overlap between observed and asymptotic dipole frequencies, represented as spike trains convolved with Gaussian kernels. After optimising this metric with a genetic algorithm, we use the best-fit parameters to perform a global assignment of the oscillation modes. We then validated the method using synthetic frequencies of RGB and CHeB stars perturbed by stellar rotation, and further tested it on four benchmark stars. Validation using perturbed synthetic frequencies shows that our method recovers over 95% of the dipole mixed modes across different evolutionary states, and this performance remains robust to spurious peaks and missing modes. For the benchmark stars, our dipole mode identification is consistent with previously published results, with mixed-mode parameter estimates typically agreeing within 1% for ${\Delta}{\Pi}$1 and 10% for ${\delta}{\nu}$rot and $q$. Our analysis demonstrates that the proposed method effectively addresses the challenges associated with the complex dipole mode spectrum. Thus, it enables automated identification of dipole mixed modes, supporting homogeneous, large-scale asteroseismic analyses of evolved stars.

papers.title: ZTF J2229+1928: A 23 Minute Eclipsing Double White Dwarf Binary
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of ZTF J2229+1928, a detached and eclipsing DA double white dwarf binary in a 23-minute orbit. The system was identified in a GPU-accelerated search of ZTF photometry and confirmed through follow-up observations with the high speed imager proto-Lightspeed on the 6.5-meter Magellan Clay telescope. Combining the proto-Lightspeed eclipse model with mass-radius relations gives component radii and masses of $R_1 = 0.0146^{+0.0009}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, $R_2 = 0.0186^{+0.0010}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, and $M_1 = 0.49^{+0.08}_{-0.07} \, M_\odot$, $M_2 = 0.37^{+0.06}_{-0.05} \, M_\odot$. Fitting the Keck/LRIS spectra gives component temperatures of approximately $11,100$ K and $8,200$ K, and scaling this model to the broadband spectral energy distribution gives a distance of $\sim965$ pc. Its short orbital period places it firmly in the millihertz gravitational-wave regime, and we estimate an expected signal-to-noise ratio $\mathrm{SNR} \approx 5.3$ with the upcoming LISA mission over its nominal four-year duration. ZTF J2229+1928 thus adds to the small but growing sample of eclipsing ultracompact binaries that will serve as important sources for future space-based gravitational-wave observatories.

papers.title: Thermodynamics within and across AdS Gauss--Bonnet holographic CFTs
papers.abstract: We study thermal competition within individual holographic conformal field theories (CFTs) and across theories with different anomaly coefficients in five-dimensional AdS Gauss--Bonnet gravity. We derive the work term conjugate to the dimensionless coupling from the boundary first law and use a common boundary clock to compare charged spherical saddles at fixed external source. Varying this source drives a first-order switch between the CFTs at the endpoints of the chosen coupling interval. In the unit-lapse cylinder clock with the zero-type-D vacuum energy, strict concavity at fixed radius reduces the global comparison to these two endpoints. The preferred coupling jumps across the coexistence line, whose slope is related to the entropy difference by a generalized Clapeyron relation. Where the Einstein endpoint itself undergoes small--large coexistence, a third saddle joins the competition and produces a kink in the cross-theory boundary. A compensating change of the external control preserves saddle ordering under finite energy shifts. Within fixed CFTs, we determine the neutral Hawking--Page line and the charged small--large black hole coexistence surface. The critical charge tends to zero at a finite coupling. The entropy gap closes with exponent one half, and the heat capacity diverges with exponent two thirds along a temperature sweep at the critical charge.

papers.title: Cross-shell excitations and the evolution of high spin states in $^{89}\mathrm{Y}$: A shell-model revisit
papers.abstract: Nuclei in the vicinity of $Z=38$--40 and $N=50$ provide an important testing ground for studying the evolution of nuclear structure across the proton subshell and neutron shell closure. In particular, $^{89}$Y offers an opportunity to investigate the inert core behaviour and effect of particle-hole excitations in generating the observed high spin states. In this work, we perform a systematic large-scale shell-model study of $^{89}$Y using different model spaces and well accepted effective interactions. Excitation energies, electromagnetic transition probabilities, and nucleon occupation probabilities are calculated and compared with available experimental data to explain the microscopic structure of the observed high spin states. The role of neutron excitations across the $N=50$ shell gap is examined in detail. A comparative analysis of the employed effective interactions is performed to assess their applicability in describing the spectroscopic properties of $^{89}$Y.

papers.title: Radiative stability of species-separated Kaluza--Klein spectra in warped geometry
papers.abstract: Species-dependent fifth-direction lightcones, generated by scalar-gradient operators, can separate gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein (KK) scales in a warped extra dimension, as recently shown by Randall and Riojas. In this work, we study whether this separation survives quantum corrections. Quark loops can only move the gluon speed within the interval spanned by the bare speeds. Gluon exchange pulls the quark speed toward the gluon speed, with a one-loop coefficient strongly enhanced by fifth-component exchange when the gluon is the slow species. We set the size of this effect using the strong-coupling estimates for a light-gluon benchmark, where a $5.5$~TeV gluon sits below quark partners at $10.74$~TeV. Within the effective theory, the Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes then correct the quark speed at order one. That correction is several times larger than the mass ordering can absorb, so the light-gluon ordering has no perturbative protection. The reverse benchmark, with slow quarks and a heavy gluon, keeps its ordering roughly ten times more robust.

papers.title: Relational Cosmology: Covariant and Canonical Dressings, and the Hamiltonian of Internal Time
papers.abstract: We compare covariant and canonical relational dressings with gauge-fixing reductions for the flat FLRW minisuperspace with a homogeneous massless scalar. We distinguish covariance of the dressing map from symmetries of the relational theory: fixing a clock makes its frame fields background structures, so its reorientations act as vector fields on relational field space rather than as spacetime diffeomorphisms. This loss of relational-time reparametrization covariance permits a nontrivial relational Hamiltonian, distinct from the undressed and dressed Hamiltonian constraints, which vanish on the constraint surface. We identify the conditions under which the dressed equations reproduce the original constrained dynamics. The relational generator defines a Hamiltonian flow even when relational-time translations are not symmetries of the dressed action. In each clock frame, it corresponds to the canonical complete observable and reduced Hamiltonian on the appropriate solution space, through the Legendre map and relational evaluation. The classical descriptions are compatible but retain distinct variational principles and intermediate phase spaces; their quantum equivalence remains an open question.

papers.title: A triple-threat challenge for $\mathit{T}$ and $\mathit{S}$ at two loops
papers.abstract: In the $Z_2$-symmetric real singlet-scalar extension of the Standard Model (SM), the oblique parameters $\mathit{T}$ and $\mathit{S}$ first receive contributions at two loops, making their precise prediction a challenge. We take on this challenge with a triple threat. First, we perform an exact two-loop calculation in the full theory. Second, we derive the logarithmically enhanced terms from a general argument, according to which the singlet rescales the Higgs couplings to the electroweak gauge bosons and thereby spoils the cancellation of ultraviolet divergences between Higgs and Goldstone contributions. Third, we reproduce the results in the SM effective field theory, where the logarithms and mass-dependent terms stem from one-loop matrix elements of the dimension-six operator that modifies the Higgs kinetic term, and the remaining constants from two-loop matching. Our calculations provide a blueprint for new-physics scenarios in which the leading effects modify the Higgs couplings in a custodially symmetric way, so that custodial-symmetry violation, and hence $\mathit{T}$, arises only beyond one loop. Finally, we derive constraints from current and projected electroweak precision measurements and show that effects beyond dimension six matter for light singlets.

papers.title: Probing the internal structure of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon via its weak decays and lifetime
papers.abstract: The weak decay properties of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon play a crucial role in probing its internal structure and guiding experimental efforts. Using an effective Lagrangian approach, we systematically study its weak decays and lifetime by computing the widths for both three- and four-body final states, with amplitudes receiving contributions from single- and double-weak-vertex diagrams. We investigate the dependence of the decay properties on the binding energy ranging from a few MeV to over $100$ MeV. For weakly bound states ($E_b = 1$ and $20$ MeV), the three-body channels $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$, $\Omega \Xi \pi$, and $\Xi \Xi \bar{K}$ exhaust essentially the entire width, with the largest channel shifting from $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$ at $E_b=1$ MeV to $\Omega \Xi \pi$ at $E_b=20$ MeV. For deeply bound states ($E_b = 100$ and $120$ MeV), the $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$ channel is forbidden, and the dominant modes are $\Omega \Xi \pi$ and $\Xi \Xi \bar{K}$, while the double-weak-vertex channel $\Lambda \bar{K} \Lambda \bar{K}$ is found to be negligibly small. As the binding energy increases, the total lifetime extends from the order of $10^{-10}~\mathrm{s}$ to $10^{-9}~\mathrm{s}$. These distinct differences in decay patterns and lifetimes provide valuable theoretical reference values for experimental searches at RHIC and the LHC, and offer a clear discriminator between the compact hexaquark and weakly bound molecular interpretations.

papers.title: Correlation Geometry and Emergent Space-Time from Stochastic Correlation Flows
papers.abstract: We propose an effective framework relating correlation geometry to stochastic flows of correlation projectors. Physical configurations are encoded by measures on spaces of self-adjoint operators, with physical equivalence defined by unitary conjugation. Assuming a smooth, spectrally separated correlation sector, local orthonormal frames define a Wilczek--Zee connection, while a Stratonovich gradient-flow ansatz preserves the projector constraints. In a local continuum approximation with massive fast modes, standard one-loop methods generate Yang--Mills-type terms and curvature terms of Einstein--Hilbert form. Along a smooth closed path, the trace of a cyclic product of projectors converges to the trace of the parallel-transport operator as the discretization is refined. We examine possible geometric, disordered, and topological regimes and motivate the stochastic dynamics through an effective open-system description. The first-order frame action defines a symplectic structure on the projector sector, providing a starting point for its relation to gravitational canonical variables. We identify the matching conditions required for an Ashtekar phase-space description and the assumptions connecting correlation geometry to induced interactions and emergent spacetime.

papers.title: The 21 cm-Lyman-$\alpha$ forest cross-power spectrum with a minimal effective field theory
papers.abstract: Intensity maps of the 21 cm line and the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly$\alpha$) forest trace the same cosmic volume at $2\lesssim z\lesssim 4$. Their cross-power spectrum is insensitive to foregrounds that do not correlate between the two probes and, together with the Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectrum, separates the mean 21 cm brightness temperature from the neutral hydrogen (HI) bias. Effective field theory models of each tracer exist, but at one loop they carry tens of nuisance parameters. We test whether a minimal effective field theory (mEFT), consisting of the tree-level Kaiser model with leading-order counterterms and stochastic terms, previously validated for the Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectrum, describes the 21 cm auto-, Ly$\alpha$ auto- and cross-power spectra jointly. We use the Sherwood 80 $h^{-1}$Mpc hydrodynamical simulation with HI painted onto halos at $z=2.4$-$4.2$, and reduce sample variance with Zel'dovich control variates. Each spectrum is validated separately and then in a joint fit with shared parameters. With scale cuts $k_{\rm max}=0.5$, $1.2$ and $2.0\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ for the 21 cm auto-, cross- and Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectra, the mEFT fits all three spectra at all five redshifts. In the joint fit the mEFT determines the HI bias to 2.0-2.5% and the Ly$\alpha$ density bias to 2.1-2.3%. The scale cuts follow the HI velocity dispersion and the Ly$\alpha$ pressure-smoothing scale. When the brightness temperature is left free, the fits that include the cross-spectrum prefer values 20-30% above the true one, at 1-2$\sigma$, while the two auto-spectra together do not constrain it. A prior on the HI bias recovers the true value of the brightness temperature.

papers.title: Self-Consistent Microscopic Description of the 146Sm Half-Life for Early Solar System Chronology
papers.abstract: The extinct \textit{p}-process radionuclide $^{146}$Sm, decaying to $^{142}$Nd, is a key short-lived chronometer for the formation and early evolution of terrestrial planets and planetesimals. However, there has been a long-standing discrepancy in both the experimental measurements and the theoretical evaluations of the $^{146}$Sm half-life. To address this, a self-consistent microscopic framework for $\alpha$ decay is developed in this work, in which the $\alpha$ particle is treated as a four-nucleon quartet. Its formation amplitude in the nuclear interior is constructed from a coherent superposition of multiple pure single-particle configurations weighted by the pairing occupation amplitudes. Coupling this shell amplitude to the $\alpha$ cluster that survives in the low-density surface region yields a self-consistently determined two-state (shell~$\oplus$~cluster) preformation weight and effective potential. The calculated half-lives for the neighboring emitters of $^{146}$Sm are in good agreement with the measured values. Cross-validation over the neighboring emitters reproduces each excluded half-life without any nucleus-specific adjustment, and yields $^{146}$Sm predictions consistent to within $\pm 6\%$ of the resulting half-life $T_{1/2}=75.1^{+6.1}_{-5.6}$~Ma. This provides a solid calibration for theoretical studies of the early solar system.

papers.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
papers.abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

papers.title: Tricritical Dynamics Reveal Black Hole Interior Geometry
papers.abstract: We reconstruct the interior Kasner exponents of a scalarized black-hole equilibrium from the growth rate of a radial perturbation outside the horizon. The equal-entropy coexistence line of Reissner--Nordstr\"om and scalarized phases ends at a tricritical point. We follow the intermediate equilibrium separating the two phases along the coexistence line. The radial growth rate $\Omega_u$ is proportional to the magnitude of the entropy-potential curvature. As the tricritical point is approached, the curvature vanishes as the fourth power of the horizon scalar amplitude. The interior logarithmic scalar gradient grows inversely with the horizon amplitude. Eliminating the amplitude connects exterior dynamics to interior geometry, giving the angular Kasner exponent $p\sim2\sqrt{\Omega_u/C}$. The static source expansion and the critical Reissner--Nordstr\"om zero mode fix $C$ before the scalarized interior is integrated. We compute the growth rate from linear radial perturbations on asymptotically flat and anti-de Sitter black-hole backgrounds. At the sampled equilibria closest to tricriticality, the reconstructed angular exponent agrees with the result of independent inward integration at about the $0.5\%$ level.

papers.title: Observation of the $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\pi^+\pi^-$ decay and an improved measurement of the $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ branching fraction
papers.abstract: An observation of the rare decay $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\pi^+\pi^-$ is reported from proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13.6 TeV, collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC in 2022 and 2023, and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.6 fb$^{-1}$. In addition, the branching fraction ratio of $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ relative to $\eta$ $\to$ $\mu^+\mu^-$ is measured with a precision improved by 44% compared with the previous measurement. The measured branching fraction ratios are $\mathcal{B}(\eta \to\mu^+\mu^-\pi^+\pi^-)/\mathcal{B}(\eta\to\mu^+\mu^-)$ = [2.89 $\pm$ 0.48 (stat) $^{+0.42}_{-0.29}$ (syst)]$\times$ 10$^{-3}$ and $\mathcal{B}(\eta\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-)/\mathcal{B}(\eta\to\mu^+\mu^-)$ = [0.86 $\pm$ 0.06 (stat) $^{+0.09}_{-0.08}$ (syst)]$\times$10$^{-3}$.

papers.title: Novel method for measuring the isovector partner of X(3872)
papers.abstract: The predicted isovector partner of the $X(3872)$, denoted as $W_{c1}$, is expected to produce only a relatively weak structure near the charged $D \bar{D}^*$ threshold, making its experimental identification challenging. In this work, we explore the triangle singularity (TS) mechanism as a means of enhancing the sensitivity to the $W_{c1}$ in the decays $B^0 \to \pi K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$. We investigate the $D_{s1}(2536) \bar{D}^*$ triangle rescattering mechanism, incorporating the coupled-channel $D \bar{D}^*$ scattering amplitudes obtained from the Lippmann-Schwinger equation. The interplay between the TS and the coupled-channel dynamics produces characteristic structures in the $K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$ invariant mass distributions associated with the $X(3872)$ and its isovector partner $W_{c1}$. In particular, the charged-channel contribution exhibits a distinct structure sensitive to the nearby $W_{c1}$ pole. Our results demonstrate that the TS mechanism provides a promising way to probe the otherwise weak manifestation of the $W_{c1}$, offering a complementary experimental strategy for searching for this predicted state at Belle II and LHCb.

papers.title: Exploring the Pion Vector Form Factor Beyond the Physical Sheet
papers.abstract: Using analyticity and unitarity, we parametrise the pion vector form factor on the first and second Riemann sheets, below the inelastic $\pi\omega$ threshold. We fit this model-independent parametrisation to the available $\tau^-\to\pi^-\pi^0\nu_\tau$ data from ALEPH, Belle, CLEO and OPAL, together with spacelike data from NA7 and JLab, and extract the pole position and couplings of the $\rho^\pm$ along with the pion charge radius and low-energy $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters. Our results are independent of external scattering input and agree with the literature; in particular, we find $M_{\rho^\pm} = 762.07\pm 0.63$ MeV and $\Gamma_{\rho^\pm} = 143.62^{+0.79}_{-0.80}$ MeV. The parametrisation is publicly available in the EOS software.

papers.title: Holographic viscous transport in scalar-coupled Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: We test horizon formulas for the shear and bulk viscosities of a holographic plasma against viscosities extracted directly from retarded stress-tensor correlators. We work in a five-dimensional Einstein-dilaton-Gauss-Bonnet model calibrated to the lattice QCD equation of state at zero baryon density. UV-finite renormalized correlators are obtained by including the required curvature and scalar counterterms, and the fluctuation equations are solved while retaining the full dependence on the Gauss-Bonnet coupling $\alpha$, without using a horizon conservation law or an entropy-production formula. For constant coupling, the horizon conserved-current calculation reproduces the boundary Kubo results in both channels. For the scalar-dependent coupling studied here, both methods find a minimum in the shear-viscosity-to-entropy-density ratio $\eta/s$. In the bulk channel, the conserved-current calculation truncated at first order in $\alpha$ yields a lower peak height in $\zeta/s$, with the peak temperature nearly unchanged relative to the boundary result. For both couplings, the unmodified Eling-Oz (EO) formula, $\zeta/s=(4\pi)^{-1}(\partial\phi_h/\partial\ln s)^2$, reproduces the boundary result for $\zeta/s$, where $\phi_h$ is the horizon value of the scalar. The prefactor $1/(4\pi)$ is thus retained even when the Gauss-Bonnet interaction shifts $\eta/s$ from this value. These results provide a direct boundary benchmark for horizon prescriptions and support the unmodified EO formula beyond constant coupling.

papers.title: Relating Short Range Correlated Pair Abundances to Electron-Scattering Cross Section Ratios
papers.abstract: We derive a coupled set of relations between inclusive and semi-exclusive nucleon-knockout electron-scattering cross-section ratios measured for any two nuclei in short-range-correlation (SRC) kinematics and the microscopic neutron-proton, (np-), proton-proton (pp-), and neutron-neutron (nn-) SRC pair populations in those nuclei. The derivation uses a factorized description of quasielastic scattering from SRC pairs and includes final-state interactions through nuclear transparency and single charge exchange. We show that the inclusive $(e,e')$, proton-knockout $(e,e'p)$, and neutron-knockout $(e,e'n)$ ratios are not independent: for any two nuclei where one is isospin symmetric ($N=Z$), two of these three observables determine the third within the model. For $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ and $^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}$, for example, the measured inclusive $(e,e')$ and proton-tagged $(e,e'p)$ ratios predict $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}/^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}(e,e'n)=1.35\pm0.07\,(\mathrm{exp})\pm0.15\,(\mathrm{model})$. A measurement of the $(e,e'n)$ ratio therefore provides a direct consistency test of the factorized pair-counting description. It also constrains the single-charge-exchange probabilities. Combining all three ratios with the two double-coincidence ratios determines the relative np-, pp-, and nn- SRC pair populations of any two nuclei. If one nucleus is isospin symmetric, any two of the three ratios suffice for the same result.

papers.title: Probing the Molecular Nature of $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$ through Their Decays
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the molecular interpretations of $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$ by studying their strong decays within the effective Lagrangian approach. We consider two possible configurations for $D_{sJ}(2860)$: an $S$-wave $D_1K$ molecule and a $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecule, while treating $D_{s3}(2860)$ as a $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecule. By fitting the LHCb-measured angular distribution and decay widths in $B_s^0\to\bar{D}^0K^-\pi^+$, we determine the molecular coupling constants and cutoff parameter $\Lambda$. Using these parameters, we calculate the total decay widths and the ratios $R$ of the partial widths into the $D^*K$ and $DK$ channels. For $D_{sJ}(2860)$, the $S$-wave $D_1K$ assignment provides a slightly better description of the measured total width than the $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ assignment. However, the combined $D_1K$ and $D^*K^*$ assignments for $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$, respectively, are disfavored by the predicted $R_{D_{s3}(2860)}$, which exceeds the experimental upper limit. In contrast, assigning both states as $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecules yields good agreement with the measured $R_{D_{s3}(2860)}$ and predicts $R_{D_{sJ}(2860)}\simeq 1.26$--$1.29$. These results favor the $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecular interpretation for both states, which can be further tested through future measurements of $R_{D_{sJ}(2860)}$.

papers.title: Light-Meson Spectroscopy at COMPASS
papers.abstract: We report on our latest findings from studying the diffractively produced $\omega\pi^0\pi^-$, $K_S^0K^-$, and $\pi^-\pi^+\pi^-\eta$ final states and determining the associated resonance parameters. A particular focus is on the signal of the lightest hybrid meson candidate with spin-exotic quantum numbers $J^{PC}=1^{-+}$, i.e. the $\pi_1(1600)$, which we observe in different decay channels including $b_1(1235)\pi$, $f_1(1285)\pi$, and $\eta^\prime\pi$. Furthermore, we highlight the observation of a supernumerary state with respect to predictions of quark models in the strange sector with $J^P=0^-$. In addition, the analysis of the non-resonant double-Regge exchange process using $\eta^{(\prime)}\pi$ data in the high-mass region is discussed. It is the first event-based likelihood fit of a double-Regge model and improves our understanding of non-resonant production mechanisms in light-meson spectroscopy.

background.title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
background.abstract: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia~3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of $P=331.52\pm0.02$ days. Our measure of the eccentricity ($e=0.9462\pm0.0017$) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia~3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia~3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet ($d \approx 35$ pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

background.title: De Sitter Gravity and Emergent Time from Fusion Matrix Product States and SYK
background.abstract: We propose a quantum-mechanical model dual to two-dimensional de Sitter (dS) gravity. It is a quantum channel, defined by a matrix product state that fuses one spin at each step, and is related to a limit of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model without chord crossings. Its simplest part is a random walk with an emergent $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry, which we identify with the symmetry of the future boundary of dS. It selects a time variable in which the walk obeys the Schwarzian action and yields the disk amplitude of dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. As the simplest case, we consider free massless scalar fields in the fixed background of dS$_2$. We find the agreement of the two-point function in the Bunch-Davies vacuum and the matching of symmetry. Our construction provides a concrete model for the dS/CFT correspondence for two-dimensional de Sitter gravity.

background.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
background.abstract: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes. Lastly, we provide a simple representation-theoretic argument regarding the recently proposed excited bound states of the model.

background.title: D(-1)/D7 bound states in supergravity
background.abstract: We construct D($-$1)/D7 bound states in Euclidean type IIB supergravity motivated by the string-theory setup of Bill\`o et al., whose open-string description realizes instantons in eight-dimensional super Yang--Mills theory. Previous supergravity constructions either left unresolved issues concerning ten-dimensional Euclidean supersymmetry or relied on partial smearing to codimension one. We classify the local codimension-two solutions by showing that the supersymmetric field equations reduce to two holomorphic functions subject to a single complex constraint. The candidate bound-state solutions require complementary D3-brane fluxes, consistent with the D7 worldvolume analysis. A particularly interesting solution has constant dilaton and connects the vacuum at infinity to a controlled scaling limit in which the geometry becomes $\mathbb R\times S^1\times\mathbb T^8$.

background.title: Infinite spin superparticles
background.abstract: We obtain infinite spin representations of the super-Poincar\'e algebra from a higher-derivative superparticle action on a super-Minkowski background in 3, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions. Super-twistor transforms are performed, and used to deduce first-quantised spectra.

background.title: Solving spectral flow in AdS$_3$: from covering maps to pencils
background.abstract: Strings in AdS$_3$ with pure NS-NS flux are described by the exactly solvable SL(2,$\mathbb{R}$) WZW model, yet correlators of winding strings, given by spectrally flowed operators, were so far known only up to three points. We obtain all of them, for any number of insertions and windings, in terms of unflowed correlators, proving the four-point conjecture of Dei and Eberhardt. The key ingredient is a pencil of rational maps from the worldsheet to the boundary which exists for generic insertion points, unwinds all insertions at once, and collapses to the covering map when the latter exists.

background.title: Cosmological Dressing Rules for Massive Scalars
background.abstract: The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation of de Sitter correlation functions comes in different guises including harmonic analysis and dressed flat space correlators. We observe that these are equivalent spectral representations of the same Sturm-Liouville problem. Starting from the latter we derive dressing rules for scalar fields of arbitrary mass with auxiliary propagators in the form of Euler integrals that are accessible to flat space diagrammatic tools.

background.title: Twisting IKKT with branes
background.abstract: Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. Beyond the two twists available at any finite $N$, which we studied in our previous work, we find five additional classes at infinite rank which require non-commuting backgrounds associated with D-branes in IIB supergravity. Together, these twists realize representatives of every equivalence class of twisting supercharges in flat-space type IIB supergravity recently classified by the first author; however, the precise form of the orbit stratification differs. This difference is related to a higher central extension of the IIB superalgebra that appears in our treatment of the IKKT model in the BV formalism. Expanding around the non-commutative backgrounds gives worldvolume theories on products of A- and B-branes, including four-dimensional BF theory on an emergent D3-brane. We relate all these twists to deformations of BCOV theory (the closed string field theory of the topological B-model) using the open-closed duality of classical string field theory. For one of the twists with Spin$(7)$ symmetry, we also show the localization of the IKKT partition function by Moore, Nekrasov, and Shatashvili can be directly reconstructed with the BV formalism, with their auxiliary field completion encoded by quadratic antifield terms. Throughout, we provide self-contained treatments of the formal techniques we employ.

background.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Calibration strategy and observations
background.abstract: This paper reviews how Euclid's top-level calibration requirements were translated into a calibration plan, how this plan is implemented and maintained during the survey, and how it performs in the current DR1 release. We show that DR1 already meets or exceeds most end-of-mission spectrophotometric calibration requirements. The construction of spectroscopically complete and pure samples relies on ongoing data acquisition for the Euclid Deep Survey, while point-spread-function modelling and shear calibration are still converging to their stringent accuracy requirements. With all DR1 data reprocessed with the DR1 pipeline configuration, more subtle effects have been detected and characterised, and correction strategies have been developed for DR2. These include improved absolute flux calibration, astrometry, charge-persistence correction, shutter effects, wavelength calibration, and spectrophotometric corrections for water-ice contamination. Finally, synthetic photometric transformations between Euclid and each of Roman, the James Webb Space Telescope, and the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope, are presented.

background.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) B: Discovery pipeline overview
background.abstract: We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.

background.title: Making Poisson {\sigma} again - an \'etude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
background.abstract: The Poisson $\sigma$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $\Sigma$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = \Sigma \times G \to \Sigma$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,\omega)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,\Pi)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = \Sigma \times M \to \Sigma$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $\Sigma$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,\Pi)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $\omega$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

background.title: The Gaia-alerted 2024--2025 brightening of V346 Nor
background.abstract: Young stellar objects (YSOs) build their final mass through a highly unsteady, episodic accretion process, often accompanied by outflow and ejection events. Objects undergoing episodic high-accretion states are known as eruptive YSOs. V346 Nor is an embedded eruptive YSO that underwent a sudden optical brightening in 2024 July that triggered an alert from the Gaia Photometric Science Alert system. With the aim of characterizing the physical processes behind this recent brightening event, we analyze new and archival photometric and spectroscopic monitoring data. We study how the brightness, colors, and spectral features changed with time in the past decade. We also fitted an accretion disk model to the observations in which the stellar mass--accretion rate product $M_{\star}\dot{M}$ and the line-of-sight extinction $A_V$ are free parameters. The accretion rate in V346 Nor has been higher ($M_{\star}\dot{M} \sim 10^{-4}\,M_{\odot}^2\,$yr$^{-1}$) since 2021 than during any previous historical peak, although it was relatively constant during the 2025 February-May brightness maximum, which was driven instead by a drop in extinction from $A_V \approx 20$\,mag to $10$\,mag. V346 Nor has accreted about 2\% of the stellar mass since its outburst. A P Cygni profile in H$\alpha$ indicates a strong outflowing wind reminiscent of classical FUors. The variability of the CaII infrared triplet lines and transient CO bandhead emission point to a highly unstable inner disk and accretion region. The persistence of forbidden line emission indicates ongoing jet activity. The brightness and color variations of V346 Nor are the result of a superposition of changes in the accretion rate and the line-of-sight extinction. With record-high accretion levels and strong wind and jet activity, V346 Nor is in one of its most active phases since its original outburst in the 1970s.

background.title: Six-Loop Renormalization in Quantum Electrodynamics
background.abstract: We analytically compute the six-loop corrections to the scale evolution of the electric charge, fermion mass, and fermion field in quantum electrodynamics. The results are obtained in the $\MSbar$ scheme for an arbitrary number of equally charged fermions. They extend renormalization in quantum electrodynamics by one loop order and allow new tests of the behavior of perturbation theory at high orders. The methods developed here also open the way to six-loop computations of renormalization in quantum chromodynamics.

background.title: Reinforcement learning to design near-perfect acoustic absorbers
background.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is proposed as a strategy for the multi-objective design of Helmholtz resonators with near-perfect acoustic absorption. The approach formulates resonator design as a sequential decision-making problem in which geometrical parameters are iteratively updated to balance competing objectives, including resonator volume, resonance frequency, and acoustic reflection. A Q-learning algorithm based on a neural network is developed to explore the design space and identify non-dominated solutions, providing a Pareto front of optimal configurations. The acoustic response is evaluated using a transfer matrix method that incorporates viscothermal losses and acoustic end corrections. Three representative designs are subsequently investigated using full-wave finite element simulations, showing good agreement in their absorption and reflection spectra and validating the accuracy of the reduced-order model. Finally, one optimized resonator is fabricated by three-dimensional printing and experimentally characterized in an impedance tube. The measured absorption coefficient reaches approximately 95\% near the resonance frequency, in agreement with the numerical predictions. These results demonstrate the potential of reinforcement learning for the automated design of compact acoustic absorbers and establish a computationally efficient framework combining multi-objective optimization, numerical modelling, and experimental validation.

background.title: Existence of a fluid phase for the two-dimensional one-component plasma
background.abstract: The two-dimensional one-component plasma is a system of point charges that repel each other logarithmically, in a uniform neutralizing background. When the inverse temperature $\beta$ is at most $2$, we prove that its correlations decay exponentially, and that its Gibbs state is unique among point processes whose fluctuations are controlled. This constitutes part of the fluid phase predicted by physicists. As a consequence, we obtain the existence of an infinite-volume limit, extending the Ginibre point process, which we call $\mathrm{Gin}_\beta$. We show that its truncated two-point function, at the scale of the Debye length, is given to first order in $\beta$ by the Debye-H\"uckel approximation.

background.title: Spectral function, OPE, and QNMs detect different singular points of black branes with unequal R-charges
background.abstract: We consider black brane solutions in the STU model, with three R-charges labeled by the parameters $q_1,q_2,q_3$. For equal R-charges $q_1=q_2=q_3$, the solution becomes the Reissner-Nordstr\"om black brane. For unequal R-charges $q_1>q_2>q_3\geq0$, there are three curvature singular points at $R\equiv r^2=-q_i$. Only $R=-q_3$ is the physical singularity, and the other two lie beyond it. Their optical times $T_i$, the complex times of null rays from the boundary to these singular points and back, form a right triangle in the complex $T$-plane. We probe these singular points using three observables, all built from the retarded correlator of $T_{xy}$ at zero spatial momentum: spectral function, OPE coefficients, and QNMs. The exponentially small correction to the spectral function at large real frequency is dominated by $T_1$ and $T_2$, which have the smallest ${\rm Im}\,T_i$. The OPE convergence radius is determined by $T_1$, which has the smallest $|T_i|$. A line of QNMs lies along the direction of $1/T_2$, since $T_2$ has the smallest phase $\arg T_i$. Furthermore, there is a second line of QNMs along the negative imaginary axis, which carries information about $T_3$ corresponding to the physical singularity. We derive these results from a WKB analysis and check them numerically. The three observables are therefore sensitive to different singular points of the geometry.

background.title: Degeneracies in the quasinormal mode spectrum of the Kerr-Sen black hole
background.abstract: The non-Hermitian nature of the eigenvalue problem underlying black hole perturbations can induce the presence of exceptional points (EPs) in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum. EPs are points in parameter space where QNMs become degenerate. Near an EP, QNMs are resonantly excited, leaving imprints on the ringdown signal. In this work, we investigate the exceptional structure of scalar perturbations of the Kerr-Sen black hole, a rotating, charged solution of the low-energy limit of heterotic string theory, and compare it with the EP structure of the Kerr-Newman black hole in General Relativity. Starting from the EP associated with a massive scalar field in the Kerr limit, we trace exceptional lines in the parameter space spanned by the black hole spin, charge, and field mass. We locate these degeneracies directly by imposing double-root conditions on the QNM secular equation, thus avoiding the need for parameter space scans. We also investigate the hysteresis phenomenon, showing that encircling an EP in parameter space leads to an exchange of the associated QNMs.

background.title: The N-Body Problem on Coadjoint Orbits
background.abstract: We show (Theorem 3) that the symplectic reduction of the spatial $n$-body problem at non-zero angular momentum is a singular symplectic space consisting of two symplectic strata, one for spatial motions and the other for planar motions. Each stratum is realized as coadjoint orbit in the dual of the Lie algebra of the linear symplectic group $Sp(2n-2)$. The planar stratum arises as the frontier upon taking the closure of the spatial stratum.
